labor-sheds.name: Labor Sheds
labor-sheds.narrative: Two numbers on this page change what a shed costs and how it performs, and neither is obvious from a photograph. The first is the floor: an RCC slab rather than a board platform is what lets a hall take dense bed rows and daily wet cleaning for years. The second is the ventilation build-up: a continuous louvre band integrated into the wall, working with a ridge ventilator, is what keeps a single large volume habitable without power. When you compare quotations line by line, compare those two first.

prefab-site-canteen.name: Prefab Site Canteen
prefab-site-canteen.narrative: Two lines in the tables below change what you actually buy. The first is that the floor and wall finishes split by zone, so a dining wall and a wash-area wall are not the same specification and are not priced as though they were. The second is that the roof exhaust package is conditional: a dining-only canteen does not inherit a heavy kitchen hood, and a canteen with a cookline needs one engineered before manufacture rather than cut in afterwards.
